basis: Mitochondrial myopathy and diabetes define disease; pyramidal dysfunction supported by Babinski sign and frequent lower-limb hyperreflexia (30-79%); neuropathy is occasional.
Chromosomal duplication syndrome defined by syndromic intellectual disability; no other common organ damage established.
Disorder of atrioventricular electrical conduction.
Renal cell carcinoma originating in the kidney.
Neuroendocrine tumor originating in the duodenum; hormone expression alone does not establish an endocrine dysfunction syndrome.
Autoimmune thyroid-centered syndrome; gastritis/celiac disease and macrocytic/pernicious anemia are constituent manifestations, each frequent (30-79%); skin findings <30%.
Primary ovarian insufficiency/dysgenesis is a defining endocrine presentation; male gametogenic failure adds no axis; cancer predisposition is a later risk.
Inherited proline metabolic disorder; additional organ involvement varies across subtypes and is not established for most patients.
Primary trigeminal autonomic headache disorder; tearing, conjunctival injection and nasal symptoms do not establish additional organ damage.
Distal arthrogryposis with muscle abnormalities, joint restriction and trismus; jaw muscle restriction does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Destructive mast-cell malignancy; hepatomegaly is frequent (30-79%), but hepatic infiltration or dysfunction is not established by enlargement alone.
Inherited disorder of skin pigmentation.
Abducens cranial neuropathy; strabismus results from nerve dysfunction rather than direct damage to the eye.
Acquired motor-neuron degeneration or injury; secondary weakness and denervation do not establish a separate primary muscle lesion.
Heterotaxy with major congenital cardiac and vascular malformations; abnormal liver position and polysplenia do not establish functional organ damage.
Neoplasm originating in the larynx, part of the airway; hormone elevations alone do not establish endocrine damage; functional hormone syndromes are very rare.
Congenital ectopic pancreatic tissue; asymptomatic location variants do not establish damage to other organs or endocrine dysfunction.
Thymic neuroendocrine carcinoma; thymus has no listed organ axis. Neuroendocrine differentiation alone establishes neither endocrinopathy nor an immune mechanism.
Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy with skeletal muscle necrosis, fatty replacement and proximal weakness.
Myopathy of the internal anal sphincter, gastrointestinal smooth muscle rather than skeletal muscle.
Gallbladder obstruction; gallbladder and bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Benign mesenchymal soft-tissue neoplasm; anatomical sites vary, so renal or pulmonary labels cannot be generalized from individual subtypes.
Congenital bladder and ureter disorder with massive vesicoureteral reflux; associated urinary infections are separately diagnosed complications.
Mitochondrial disorder with cardiomyopathy (4/4); hepatic injury in ~75-80%; developmental delay is defining (1/1 annotated). Nephritis reported once; evidence insufficient beyond four-axis cap.
Francisella infection localized to lymph nodes; lymph-node involvement alone does not establish blood-cell, marrow or coagulation disease.
